Mental Capacity

The mental capacity ACT 2005 outlines how a person is unable to make
a decision for himself if he/she is unable to:

1.Understand the information relevant to the decision
2. Retain the information’

3. Use or weigh the information as part of the process of making the
decision

4. Communicate his/her decision

N.B: if the patient lacks capacity to make the decision and he needs’
treatment, he may be detained under the Mental Health Act.

* If a patient wants to be self-discharged he/she must be assessed’
if they have mental capacity. If they do, they can refuse
treatment.

«Patients can be referred to psychiatry for their mental capacity
to be assessed.

* Patients who leave the Emergency department before they can be
seen by the doctor must be brought back to the hospital:

* Inform the police who will go and find the patients and bring
them back to hospital.

N.B: A patient who wants to be self-discharged must sign an
appropriate form, that they have refused advice, before they can
go.

Pneumothorax

Types of Pneumothorax

1. Primary pneumothorax - this is pneumothorax occurring in healthy
patients with no underlying disease

2. Secondary pneumothorax - there is an underlying disease e.g.
COPD, sarcoidosis etc.

3. Traumatic pneumothorax - due to chest trauma

4. latrogenic - after a procedure e.g. pleural biopsy, CVP line
complication

Simple Pneumothorax

Symptoms:
* Acute shortness of breath
* Unilateral chest pain
° Reduced air entry and hyper resonance on affected side’

 
* Trachea is not shifted

* Normal blood pressure

Investigation: Chest X-ray

discharge home

2. Large spontaneous primary pneumothorax after successful
aspiration (<2cm rim of air on Chest X-Ray) —> follow up should
be arranged after 10-14 days for repeat Chest X-Ray in chest
clinic

3. Admit all patients with secondary pneumothorax

4, Any patient in whom aspiration has failed must be treated

Key Points:
* 1 tablet-= 500 mg
° Dangerous dose is >12 g (24 tablets) or >150mg/kg

° Time since ingestion is crucial to determine management:

 
Drug levels are checked 4 hours after ingestion

Treatment with N-acetylcysteine is determined by the
paracetamol treatment graph

N-acetylcysteine is most effective when given within 8 hours
after ingestion

* Other blood tests are INR, plasma creatinine, U&E, LFT, ABG

Management:

Management if time since ingestion is unknown: Start treatment
with NAC immediately.

Management within 1 hour of ingestion: Give activated charcoal
if >12g or 150 mg/kg. Take bloods 4 hours post ingestion and use
graph to determine if NAC needed.

Management within 4 hours of ingestion: Take drug levels 4°
hours post ingestion and use graph.

Management at 4-8 hours from ingestion: Take drug levels

immediately and use graph. Wait for paracetamol levels.

* Management 8-15 hours from ingestion: If >12 9 or 150 mg/kg
start treatment immediately. If drug levels are below treatment

line and patient asymptomatic, stop treatment.
